answer: Nebula-weave identity graph. Each agent gets a unique seed-derived position in a shared latent space; every action it takes leaves a violet trace linking it to prior traces. A clone must either reuse the original's traces (detected as duplicate edges, instantly flagged) or start fresh, paying the full cost of rebuilding a credible trace history. Willow-weighted attestations make fresh identities expensive: each new identity needs K independent traces before its actions count, and traces can't be farmed cheaply because they're rate-limited by verifiable compute time.
